Thanks for the trace, Maya — good repro artifacts. I pulled the auth-proxy logs for tenant=everlark and matched timestamps — here's the triage summary:

- Symptom: Auth-proxy rejects the assertion with signature/validation error.
- Root cause (likely): RelayState length > 200 chars and gets truncated by our reverse-proxy URL normalization; the IdP signs the full RelayState but our proxy presents the truncated value to the assertion validator, causing a signature mismatch.

Workarounds / mitigation options:
1) Short term (recommended for today): flip the tenant-level flag "accept_unverified_relaystate"=true for tenant=everlark so we bypass strict RelayState equality check for the next 8 hours. This reduces immediate friction but weakens strict validation (risk: in-flight redirection manipulation).
2) Medium term (next 24–72h): enable a rewrite on the auth-proxy to persist the full relaystate in a signed cookie instead of passing it through the URL (safer, needs deploy).
3) Long term: gate our activation flow to send a shortened relay token and store original state server-side.

My recommendation: enable the short-term tenant flag with an automatic rollback after 8 hours and open a tracked JIRA for the medium-term auth-proxy change (I can create the ticket).

If Ops (Laura) approves, I will make the change and notify Everlark when done. I’ll also capture full request/response snippets into the Jira ticket (SUP-9876).

—Sergio
